messages.author: 6d1317ea0c22cc59
messages.subject: Multi-level Bayesian Framework using Arrays of Different Dimensions
parts:
I am interested in a multi-level Bayesian framework using arrays of different dimensions. For example, a meta-analysis of M studies where each study has N_m different individuals and K_m factors of interest. I get the following error:

Error in data_list2array(x) : 
  the dimensions for all elements (array) of the list are not same
failed to preprocess the data; sampling not done

leading me to believe Stan is not able to process arrays of different dimensions (though I did not see this explicitly stated in the User's Guide). The imported data arrays are: x = (list(x,x2,x3)),  y=(list(y,y2,y3)) , g = (list(matrix, matrix2, matrix3)), where 'list' is being used to combine vectors/matrices of different lengths. Thanks, let me know if the question is unclear.

cause_code_meta <- 'data{
int M;
int O;
int N[M];
int K[M];
real x[N[M],O,M];
real y[N[M],O,M];
real g[N[M],K[M],M];
}
parameters {
real beta0[M];
real beta1[M];
real beta1_causal;
real alpha0[M];
real alpha[K[M],M];
real sigmax[M];
real sigmay[M];
real si;
}
transformed parameters {
real xi[N[M],M];
real eta[N[M],M];
real alphak[N[M],K[M]];
for(m in 1:M) {
for(i in 1:N[m]) {
for(k in 1:K[m]) {
alphak[i,k] <- alpha[k,m]*g[i,k,m];
}
xi[i,m] <- alpha0[m] + sum(alphak[i]);
eta[i,m] <- beta0[m] + beta1[m]*xi[i,m];
}
}
}
model {
beta0[M] ~ normal(0,100);
beta1[M] ~ normal(beta1_causal,si);
si~uniform(0,1000);
alpha0[M] ~ normal(0,100);
alpha[K[M],M] ~ normal(0,100);
sigmax[M] ~ uniform(0,1000);
sigmay[M] ~ uniform(0,1000);
for(m in 1:M) {
for(i in 1:N[m]) {
x[i,m] ~ normal(xi[i,m], sigmax[m]);
y[i,m] ~ normal(eta[i,m], sigmay[m]);
}
}
}
'

cause_data_meta <- list(M = 3, O =1, N = c(N, N2, N3), K = c(3, 1, 2),  x = (list(x,x2,x3)),  y=(list(y,y2,y3)) , g = (list(matrix, matrix2, matrix3)))
fit_cause_meta <- stan(model_code = cause_code_meta, data = cause_data_meta, iter = 1000, chains = 4)

For those interested, this question/formulation is motivated by Burgess S., Thompson S. & CRP CHD Genetics Collaboration. Bayesian methods for meta-analysis of causal relationships estimated using genetic instrumental variables. Statist. Med. 2010, 29: 1298-1311.

You are right about not support ragged arrays. I do not think it makes sense in Stan to declare data as you did though stanc does not complain.   RStan reports error when dealing with a list of elements with different dimensions since that is not supported by Stan. 

Jiqiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Multi-level Bayesian Framework using Arrays of Different Dimensions
parts:
We've been planning to add ragged arrays, but haven't yet.
The C++ structure for arrays is a std::vector, so there's
no problem modifying it for ragged arrays. Sparse vectors
and matrices will eventually be added as new basic datatypes,
along with other structured types (next to be rolled out is
Cholesky factor for correlation matrices).

We should make it clearer in the manual(s) that we don't
support them now --- as is, it's only implicit in that the enumeration
of things we do support are all non-ragged.

In the manual, in the chapter on clustering, in the section on naive Bayes,
there's a subsection titled "Representing Ragged Arrays in Stan".
This is the kind of organization Herra Huu is suggesting.
We also use it for things like IRT models when not every
student gets every question on the test or Bradley-Terry
models for non-round-robin tournaments. And you can use
it for sparse matrices, as well, but we don't yet support
any sparse matrix operations.

- Bob
